ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, legal representatives and managers against: (a) Luxembourg CSSF consolidated lists and national FIU references; (b) UN and EU consolidated sanctions lists; (c) OFAC SDN list for any USD-clearing or cross-border transactions; (d) PEP databases maintained by internationally recognized providers; enhanced due diligence required for any PEP or politically exposed connection; ongoing transaction monitoring under the amended Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS), online via lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in Latin script using Luxembourgish, French, or German orthography; the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' is mandatory; names must not be misleading, confusingly similar to existing registered names, nor contrary to French/German/Luxembourgish linguistic norms; accent marks are allowed but transliteration to standard Latin characters is required if not in the national language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative complaint with the RCS registry (service de l'immatriculation des sociétés) no later than 15 days from rejection; attach a negative search report and, where the name contains a sensitive token, a ministerial authorization from the Ministry of Justice or the responsible sectoral authority (e.g., Ministry of Health for clinical/EMR terms); if the registry confirms rejection, an appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal Administratif within three months, represented by a Luxembourg-qualified counsel; the name reservation may be renewed once for an additional period upon payment of the prevailing renewal tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible in Luxembourg for a low-risk software entity, provided that the virtual office provider can accept service of process and maintain the company's registered seat documents at a physical address in Luxembourg. However, for a healthcare/EMR SaaS activity, the RCS and tax administration will scrutinize actual substance; a virtual office alone may be insufficient to prove effective management, place of effective management, or VAT establishment. It is advisable to maintain a Luxembourg premises or an administrative service provider with full substance support.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-low quantitative risk: approximately 15% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection during the first two years, triggered by incomplete UBO filings, material discrepancies in commercial registers, or sectoral healthcare-licensing concerns; RCS and the FIU may conduct on-site inspections under AML/CFT procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 100-101 for SARL formation; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with coordinated Articles of Association (statuts coordonnés)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and fully paid-up capital for a SARL is EUR 12,000; the fully paid-up capital must be deposited in a bank account in Luxembourg in the name of the company or to the order of the notary before signature, with a blocking certificate issued by the financial institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators hereby subscribe to the fully paid-up share capital of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée as set forth in the articles of association, each share being subscribed for cash, and such capital shall be deposited in escrow prior to the signature of the notarial deed. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is established at the address stated in the articles of association and that the company's RCS application be filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] are appointed as managers (gérants) with joint representation authority, each with the corporate power to execute all operational and banking formalities. RESOLVED, that the managers are instructed to complete all statutory registration, publication, trade licensing, and health-IT authorisation filings on behalf of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through the online platform of the Ministère des Finances / LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a written request for reservation of the corporate name. The reservation is made exclusively for the SARL legal form, validated against Luxembourg company registers and trademark databases, and is valid for two months. Notarise the reservation form if required by the selected mode of filing; otherwise submit digitally with an authenticated signature.
required_dossiers: Corporate object description, including ISIC 6201 and health-IT software services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, submit a new name and re-file the reservation. If the RCS queries the object description, amend the corporate object clause to align with ISIC 6201 and the Luxembourg health data processing legislation before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) approved for notary funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account or use a notary escrow sub-account. Transfer fully paid-up share capital of at least EUR 12,000. Obtain a certificate of blocked funds confirming the account is blocked in favour of the notary for incorporation purposes; the certificate is delivered to the notary on the date of deed signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses deposit due to KYC deficiencies, correct the beneficial owner declarations and resubmit the file. If the capital shortfall is identified, the subscriber must complete the missing amount to EUR 12,000 before the notary signs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) practising before the Court of First Instance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the draft articles and all capital evidence with the notary. The notary verifies the legal capacity of subscribers, validates the minimum capital requirement and block certificate, and signs the notarial deed with all subscribers present or represented by power of attorney. The notary then obtains the Company's first RCS extract
required_dossiers: Passports or ID cards of subscribers and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests additional information or corrections, the subscribers amend the draft deed and re-notarise. Any delay in receiving the blocking certificate is cured by obtaining an updated certificate in the name of the same notary file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), Service du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After deed signature, the notary files the incorporation file electronically with the RCS. The RCS assigns the company registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and issues the legal certificate. The application must be submitted within one month of the deed date. The RCS also uploads the deed and articles to the electronic register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised, the notary corrects the filing within the eight-day RCS response window. If the register requests a restated corporate object, the general meeting of shareholders adopts an extraordinary resolution and the amended articles are filed for approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Formation and Appointment of Managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Journal / Legilux, and the RCS daily register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS publishes the formation notice and the representative powers of the managers in the electronic compendium. The notice is entered in the Official Journal of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Legilux). No further fee is payable by the company if the publication is effected by the RCS; the publication notification is automatically recorded in the RCS extract.
required_dossiers: Company legal form, name, registered office, object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication errors occur, request rectification immediately from the RCS with the authenticated direct debit; if no publication is recorded, ask the notary to issue a formal notification to the RCS for publication in the next available daily register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé) and the Luxembourg Data Protection Authority (Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données, CNPD) for health-data-related activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de traitement de données relatives à la santé / Compliance certification for EMR SaaS clinical workflow software under the Act of 1 August 2018 on the protection of health data

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-exempt class for the conduct of a purely digital software service; no full EIA report is required absent physical laboratories, clinical storage, or significant waste discharges
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If the licensed premises hosts servers or backup power equipment, no industrial wastewater or VOC thresholds apply; electronic equipment must comply with the EU WEEE Directive and the Luxembourg regulation on waste electrical and electronic equipment. Only negligible office-generated municipal waste and confidential-data destruction via approved contractors are permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) delivered by the Grand Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps after inspection of the office and any server room; structural load inspection for server cabinets and data racks; workplace health and safety clearance issued by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering occupational risk assessment and the statement of the internal or shared prevention service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct and corporate income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) as the national company and RCS registry; official business and tax portals include guichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu and lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LU SARL first obtains a national business identification number (matricule) through RCS/LBR after notarial or e-formation registration; the RCS/LBR transmits the registration data to the tax administrations. Before commencing taxable activity, the company must apply for VAT registration through the guichet.lu professional portal or by written application to AEDT, generally within 15 days of the start of activity, attaching the RCS excerpt, constitutional documents, manager and shareholder identification, place of business evidence, ownership details and projected turnover. AEDT then issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (TVA ID in LU format). If the company will make customs-export declarations, an EORI number is also required. A non-resident SaaS vendor without an EU establishment may be required to register directly for Luxembourg VAT and may be obliged to appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative where the relevant simplified registration conditions are not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box system; entity classification follows the civil-law legal form, and an SARL is a taxable opaque entity resident in Luxembourg, not eligible for pass-through treatment. The principal statutory tax elections available include the fiscal unity regime (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR, whereby a 95%-owned Luxembourg subgroup may elect consolidated treatment for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, with the election being binding for five years; the IP box election for qualifying intellectual property income; notional interest deduction notification; and the VAT option to tax real estate. ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules apply to cross-border structures and do not create elective pass-through classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_note: A Luxembourg-resident SARL is subject to worldwide taxation on its income, with foreign tax credit relief available under applicable tax treaties; the entity-level classification extends to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover, being the current statutory small-enterprise VAT franchise threshold for Luxembourg-established businesses; a non-established foreign EMR SaaS provider supplying into Luxembourg has no turnover threshold and must register from its first taxable supply in Luxembourg, and the EU EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold may apply separately to distance sales and electronically supplied services supplied to EU consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently does not impose mandatory real-time B2B fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction controls for VAT purposes; invoices, including electronic invoices, must preserve authenticity, integrity and legibility under the Luxembourg VAT Law. B2G electronic invoicing to Luxembourg public bodies is mandatory under EU Directive 2014/55/EU and is exchanged through the Luxembourg PEPPOL BIS/eFIA environment. VAT returns, recapitulative statements, Intrastat filings and OSS returns must be submitted electronically, and complete invoice audit files must be available to AEDT upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union may be zero-rated at 0% VAT if the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside EU territory by or on behalf of the Luxembourg seller, and the seller obtains and retains proof of export within the period required by AEDT practice, generally within 90 days from the supply. For medical EMR SaaS and other digital services, the place-of-supply rules generally remove the supply from Luxembourg VAT rather than applying an export zero rate: B2B supplies to a non-EU taxable business are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT; B2B supplies to an EU taxable business are reverse-charged to the customer; B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT jurisdiction; and B2C supplies to EU consumers may be taxed through the OSS mechanism. To support 0% or outside-scope treatment, the EMR SaaS contract must identify the customer's business establishment, the service recipient's VAT/tax status, and the place of use or enjoyment, and the invoice must contain all statutory minimum particulars.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated customs export declaration (IE-529 or equivalent electronic export file released by Luxembourg/EU customs), evidencing departure to a non-EU destination and the Luxembourg seller's EORI status

Transport document, being the signed Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note, showing the Luxembourg entity as exporter/shipper and the non-EU customer as consignee or destination receiver
Inward remittance certificate, comprising bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103, or equivalent foreign-exchange receipt document evidencing payment from the foreign buyer in convertible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may reassess a zero-rated export where proof of export, transport or inward remittance is deficient, fraudulent or inconsistent. The standard limitation period for VAT assessment is five years, extended to ten years where fraud, omission or false declarations are established. Reassessment reverses the 0% rate and applies Luxembourg VAT at the standard 17% rate together with late-payment interest; administrative fines may reach up to twice the tax evaded, and criminal sanctions, including fines and imprisonment, apply for knowingly false documentation or forged export evidence. Any input VAT previously attributed to the failed zero-rating claim is retrospectively clawed back in the same assessment. The complete customs and remittance file must be preserved in the AEDT audit archive for a minimum of ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank and competes with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking oversight; however, Luxembourg is a euro-area member and foreign exchange policy is primarily harmonized under the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB). No separate Luxembourg foreign exchange administration or capital-control licensing authority exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg treats the euro as fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital (Articles 63–66 TFEU) and the EU Capital Requirements Regulation protect unrestricted cross-border payments, trade financing, and repatriation of profits, dividends, and liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance from an LU SARL is subject only to ordinary corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax (15% standard, reduced under tax treaties), not to convertibility or prior authorization hurdles. The BCL does not impose exchange controls, surrender requirements, or open-position limits on resident non-financial corporations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or regulatory repatriation timelines in Luxembourg. Export receipts denominated in foreign currency may be retained in commercial accounts, sold freely, or used to settle foreign trade obligations. The BCL only requires statistical reporting under the Balance of Payments (BoP) framework for cross-border payments exceeding de minimis thresholds; such reporting is satisfied through the resident bank's automatic transmission of transaction data and does not affect timing or use of proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Blocked Account
Operational Account, Capital Escrow Account, and Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account and Multicurrency Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium to Low for a Luxembourg SARL's primary treasury relationship. A UI (user-interface) digital EMI chartered outside the EEA is not viable for statutory share capital blocking or high-value operational settlements because Luxembourg CSSF-authorized banks must hold the legal capital account until registration. EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions may be used for low-value client collections and SaaS subscription disbursements under the EU payment services passport, but they are not substitutes for a full-service Luxembourg banking relationship covering trade finance, FX hedging, and shareholder distributions. Offshore EMIs pose compliance risk because they generally lack ISO 20022 SEPA-native clearing, corporate KYC infrastructure, and CSSF regulatory standing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated LU SARL, at least one authorized director-shareholder and the bank signatories are generally required to attend a physical onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg office. Remote video identification is accepted by most Luxembourg banks for natural persons under the CSSF-sanctioned electronic identification procedure, but the corporate legal entity must be authenticated through certified extracts from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must be identified. Foreign directors without an EU/EEA national ID may be asked to appear before the bank's compliance officers or produce a notarized and apostilled power of attorney together with a live video verification. For high-risk or complex cross-border structures fully remote onboarding is typically rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU shareholder jurisdiction scoring elevated by the bank's country risk model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity chart with certified RCS extract; legal opinion from the shareholder's home jurisdiction confirming corporate existence and source of funds; board resolution approving capital injection; shareholder shareholder's audited financial statements or bank reference letter; notarized AML representation letter; beneficial ownership declaration for every natural person above 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: HealthTech SaaS revenue model with perceived data-privacy exposure in the medical sector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 27001 certification; SOC 2 Type II report; CNPD data-processing registration or DPO appointment; EU-GDPR compliance policy; DPIA covering EMR clinical data; professional liability insurance; signed customer contracts demonstrating the software is not a provider of regulated medical services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate inbound capital relative to projected revenue from a newly opened EMR clinical license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 24-month cash-flow forecast; intercompany or shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length interest; TP documentation and robustness of transfer pricing policy; invoice pipeline from healthcare clients; evidence of statutory healthtech license or CE conformity; cumulative source-of-wealth disclosure for all contributing shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Asset-freezing or PEP (politically exposed person) flags on intermediaries or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions screening reports from a recognized database; PEP status declaration with legitimate wealth explanation; professional references from a CSSF-regulated lawyer or notary; certified copies of passports; independent financial records; commitment to ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds documentation for any future extraordinary deposits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital wires must be routed through SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg bank's euro clearing account. The payment should reference the shareholder loan or capital subscription documentation and use the ISO 20022 remittance information for transparent classification. Purpose codes in the SWIFT field 72 or 77T must align with EU BoP statistical categories: for subscribed share capital use code 'D.992' or 'ECU' depending on bank preference; for shareholder loans use 'D.161' with supporting board resolution. Verification includes confirmation of the originator's bank and country, reconciliation of the amount to the share-capital blocking certificate, and generation of a BCL external-assets/liabilities report. To prevent misclassification, instruct the remitting bank to state 'INCREASE OF SHARE CAPITAL' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' in the payment details, attach the RCS excerpt and notarized signatures, and record the funds as an escrow deposit capable of release only after notarization and RCS registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For vendor payments and SaaS infrastructure costs, the primary clearing rails are SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for euro-zone beneficiaries and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA trade settlements. Commercial letters of credit (documentary credits) are recommended for significant cross-border procurement of medical hardware or software development services; these should be denominated in EUR under UCP 600 rules, issued via the Luxembourg relationship bank, and matched against transport, insurance, and acceptance documentation to preserve clean FX settlement. Payment under the LC must be routed through the issuing bank's SWIFT MT700/MT400 messaging. Same-day euro clearing is available via TARGET2, while intra-SEPA payments are automatic. For mixed EUR/USD operational expenditure, the SARL should maintain a USD settlement sub-account with a standing currency-conversion instruction to carry only minimal FX exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (maturity ≤ 12 months, no premium leverage) against EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, and EUR/GBP for invoice sterilization

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) as an exception for emerging-market currencies without offshore deliverability (e.g., KRW, CNY, INR where local law prohibits full convertibility), with master agreement governed by Luxembourg or English law and netting under ISDA 2002
Cross-currency swaps for long-term shareholder loans or healthcare-platform capital investments to fix EUR interest and currency exposure for periods exceeding two years
FX options (vanilla European style) limited to protective purchase of USD call/EUR put for high-uncertainty revenue cycles, subject to the SARL board's derivative-risk policy
Perfectly matched back-to-back forwards on the same currency pair with a single Luxembourg bank, allowing micro-hedging of specific commercial invoices without residual open FX positions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% headline corporate income tax (IRC) for fiscal year 2024; adding the 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC (effective 18.19%) and the municipal business tax (impot commercial communal, 6.75% in Luxembourg City) produces an aggregate statutory burden of approximately 24.94% for a Luxembourg City SARL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income under the OECD-modified Nexus approach for qualifying software copyrights of the EMR platform, yielding an effective rate of approximately 5% on licensing and SaaS IP income. Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% held for 12 months. ATAD-compliant interest limitation rule caps deductible net interest at the higher of 30% of EBITDA or EUR 3,000,000. R&D tax credit available on eligible research expenditures. Loss carryforward is subject to the anti-loss-trading continuity rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg corporate income tax return: Form 610C (Declaration for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax). Electronic submission through the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) secure e-filing portal via MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed no later than 31 December of the calendar year following the close of the fiscal year (e.g., the return for fiscal year ending 31 December 2024 is due by 31 December 2025). The ACD may grant an extension, commonly until 30 June of the following calendar year, upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, RCS Luxembourg registration number, tax file number, fiscal year-end date, and status of the SARL's shareholder registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident SARL files under its Luxembourg identification; non-resident shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners are not entered on the 610C form but must be disclosed through the separate RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) filing and any applicable Country-by-Country notification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit per the statutory financial statements, reconciled to taxable income via add-backs and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All EMR SaaS revenue collected through Stripe Billing and bank transfers from foreign and domestic clinics must be included gross in commercial profit; offshore accumulation of subscription receivables without recognition constitutes fraudulent omission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible items, including the corporate income tax itself, fines, 50% of managing director remuneration, excessive interest, and undocumented intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees paid to foreign group companies are deductible only upon production of arm's length documentation under Article 56 LIR; absent substantiation, the ACD will reintegrate the charge and impose penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1D — IP box and participation exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 80% IP Box deduction on net qualifying IP income subject to the nexus ratio, and the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IP Box deduction for the EMR software copyright is available only where the qualifying R&D expenditure is incurred by the Luxembourg SARL and the Nexus ratio is documented; outsourcing development to a foreign parent without substance invalidates the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income, subject to the statutory continuity and anti-loss-trading conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border surrender of losses is not available except through Luxembourg fiscal unity (integration fiscale), which requires 95% ownership by a Luxembourg-incorporated parent; losses of foreign affiliates cannot be set off in the SARL return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1F — Municipal business tax and net wealth tax bases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recalculation of the municipal business tax base (including the 5% disallowance on participation-exempt dividend income) and declaration of taxable net wealth after the EUR 500,000 allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Municipal business tax applies only to the Luxembourg permanent establishment; non-resident-owned assets held outside Luxembourg remain outside the net wealth tax base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a coercive fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 1,500 per return plus periodic daily penalties until submission. Late payment attracts default interest of 0.6% per month. Negligent under-declaration is penalised at 10% to 50% of the reassessed tax, rising to up to 100% for gross negligence or fraud. Criminal prosecution may result in fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by a SARL to non-resident shareholders. A 0% rate applies to qualifying distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds a direct shareholding of at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12 months. Double tax treaty rates for portfolio shareholders typically range from 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Luxembourg withholding tax is levied at source on distributions. Reduced treaty rates are obtained either (i) through prior authorisation from the ACD upon submission of the non-resident beneficial owner's Certificate of Fiscal Residence (Tax Residence Certificate) and evidence of shareholding, or (ii) by filing a refund claim with the ACD on the standard restitution form within five years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld. The refund file must include the dividend resolution, bank attestation of the distribution, TRC, and a declaration of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate of 0% for both outbound royalties and interest paid by a Luxembourg SARL; Luxembourg imposes no general withholding tax on interest or licence fees paid to non-residents. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive provides a 0% rate for qualifying related-company payments. Residual double tax treaty rates on outbound royalties and interest, where a source tax exists in the other contracting state, are typically 0% to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory local file or master file threshold exists in Luxembourg. A mandatory Country-by-Country Report applies to Luxembourg ultimate parents or surrogate filing entities of multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, due within 12 months of fiscal year-end. For all cross-border controlled transactions, including EMR SaaS licensing fees and IT development services, contemporaneous Article 56 LIR transfer pricing documentation must nevertheless be available upon request; failure to produce it exposes the SARL to an arm's length adjustment, denial of deduction, and penalty surcharges.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations code. Substance is instead enforced through Article 56 LIR (arm's length principle), the anti-abuse doctrine under section 6 of the Abgabenordnung, ATAD CFC and anti-hybrid rules, OECD Nexus requirements for the IP Box, and beneficial-ownership conditions under tax treaties and EU directives. The EMR SaaS SARL must evidence genuine local presence, including board decisions taken in Luxembourg, qualified staff managing the SaaS contract book and IP exploitation, physical premises, and local bank accounts. A letterbox structure would be denied IP Box, treaty, and Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits and recharacterised as an abusive conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematic omission of EMR subscription revenue settled through Stripe Billing and international bank transfers; issuance of circular invoices to foreign affiliates to deflate the Luxembourg taxable profit; falsification of the Form 610C annexes or accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD reassessment with a penalty surcharge of 50% of the evaded tax for deliberate omission, rising to 100% for fraudulent manoeuvres, plus default interest of 0.6% per month. Criminal prosecution for fiscal fraud carries fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, together with publication of the conviction and exclusion from public tenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director (gerant) and beneficial owners may face veil-piercing for simulation and fraud, becoming jointly and severally liable for the underpaid corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and penalties. Criminal conviction may trigger a ban on leaving Luxembourg pending payment of the tax debt and disqualification from holding directorship positions in Luxembourg entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Letterbox Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL holds EMR software licences and invoices SaaS revenue without employees, premises, or operational oversight in Luxembourg, while all development, contracting, and strategic decisions are performed by the foreign parent or group companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of reported IP royalty and SaaS income as constructive distributions to the foreign shareholder, triggering a 15% withholding tax recapture and loss of the 80% IP Box exemption; penalty of 25% to 50% of the reassessed tax; deregistration from the Luxembourg RCS and refusal to issue tax residence certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gerant is personally liable for the withholding tax that should have been collected on recharacterised distributions. Civil clawback actions may be brought in insolvency proceedings, and criminal sanctions under section 6 Abgabenordnung may include travel restrictions, asset freezes, and confiscation of the diverted EMR revenues.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Synthetic Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Year-end retroactive price adjustments on EMR software licences, persistent losses by the Luxembourg SARL while the group remains highly profitable, unilateral cost bearing without risk compensation, absence of contemporaneous functional and cost analyses, and failure to prepare or produce Article 56 LIR documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 56 LIR primary transfer pricing adjustment with default interest at 0.6% per month; denial of deduction for non-substantiated intercompany fees; penalty of 10% to 50% of the reassessed tax, increased to 100% for gross negligence; notification of the adjustment to treaty partners under mutual agreement procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing directors face personal fines for knowingly participating in false transfer pricing documentation; bank account garnishment and seizure of personal assets may follow a TP-driven insolvency, and the commercial court may impose personal bankruptcy prohibition (faillite personnelle) for negligent management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the beneficial ownership declaration with the Luxembourg Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) within one month of incorporation or any ownership change; concealment of the ultimate shareholder of the non-resident holding chain; inadequate AML/KYC controls over downstream clinic subscription payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Escalating administrative fines imposed by the RBE registrar and the CSSF, including coercive daily penalties (astreinte) up to EUR 250 per day until the declaration is made; criminal fines for knowingly false UBO declarations; suspension of shareholder rights and distribution payments in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De jure directors and the designated compliance officer are personally fined for obstruction of the registrar; imprisonment of up to 5 years may apply where the EMR subscription cash flows are used to disguise proceeds of crime, and travel bans may be imposed during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT, Payroll, and Social Security Leakage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register for and file Luxembourg VAT returns on local medical-clinic EMR subscriptions (standard Luxembourg VAT rate 16%), misclassifying SaaS as an exempt medical service, or failing to operate payroll withholding and social security contributions for Luxembourg-resident staff.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate enforced recovery of unpaid VAT and payroll taxes, default interest of 0.6% per month, late-filing fines up to EUR 1,500, and VAT reassessment penalties up to 10% per quarter; criminal exposure for fraudulent misappropriation of client-withheld amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for taxes withheld from employees or collected from clients where funds are diverted to the parent company; the insolvency administrator may pursue civil restitution, and criminal courts may impose travel bans and custodial sentences for misappropriation of public monies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Health Data Protection and Statutory Licensing Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of Electronic Medical Record clinical workflow software without the required Luxembourg health-sector authorization, and processing of special-category health data of clinic patients without a valid GDPR Article 9 basis or appropriate technical safeguards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CNPD (Luxembourg data protection authority) administrative fines up to EUR 20,000,000 or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher; complementary criminal sanctions and suspension of the medical software service pending compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chairpersons and data protection officers may face personal fines and criminal liability for unlawful processing of health data; travel bans and prohibition from exercising commercial activity may accompany criminal convictions for serious GDPR breaches affecting patient safety.
